sources.supports: Every write validates its identifiers, an entry identifier through the UUID validator, places them as the path segments of the matching endpoint and forwards the JSON payload unchanged. The replies are parsed advisorily against PlanSchema, PlanEntrySchema or RunSchema.

AddPlanPayloadSchema requires name and accepts description, milestone_id, start_on, due_on, refs and an entries array. An entry carries suite_id, name, description, assignedto_id, include_all, case_ids, config_ids, a runs array, dynamic_filters, start_on, due_on and refs; a nested run carries name, description, assignedto_id, include_all, case_ids, config_ids and refs. AddPlanEntryPayloadSchema matches an entry. UpdatePlanEntryPayloadSchema omits config_ids and runs, which TestRail does not accept, and suite_id, which the endpoint's request body does not carry. AddRunToPlanEntryPayloadSchema requires config_ids and omits name, which TestRail derives from the configuration; UpdateRunInPlanEntryPayloadSchema omits both. No payload is parsed by the public method, so every payload rule is enforced at the MCP boundary alone.
zObject uses passthrough, so the declared payload types admit unknown properties; the MCP boundary must reject them separately.

add_plan requires name and accepts description, milestone_id, start_on, due_on and an entries array. add_plan_entry takes suite_id, required for projects with multiple suites or baseline support, plus name, description, assignedto_id, include_all, case_ids, config_ids, refs, start_on, due_on and runs; its top-level config_ids lists the combined configurations for the entry's runs, and every configuration a nested run names must appear in it, each run naming one full combination with one configuration per group. The reference states that config_ids and runs are not supported on update_plan_entry. add_run_to_plan_entry requires config_ids and takes description, assignedto_id, start_on, due_on, include_all, case_ids and refs; TestRail derives the run's name from its configuration.

input_policy.notes: Strictness is an MCP boundary requirement, and here it is the only enforcement: the driver forwards this payload without parsing it. Three fields an entry otherwise carries are refused rather than sent: TestRail's reference states that config_ids and runs are not supported here, and the endpoint's request body carries no suite_id. Forwarding any of them would be a silently ignored write.

outer_result.notes: TestRail answers with the updated entry and the runs it holds, returned as the driver received it; entity-field drift is advisory.

requirements.description: Reject unknown top-level fields before driver invocation rather than forwarding or discarding them.
Reject an unknown field of the entry, including one that belongs to the plan rather than the entry.
Reject config_ids, which TestRail's reference states this endpoint does not support. Accepting it would report a configuration change that never happened.
Reject runs, which TestRail's reference states this endpoint does not support. A run is changed or removed through its own tool.
Reject suite_id, which this endpoint's request body does not carry. An entry's suite is fixed when the entry is created.

parameters.semantics: The plan the entry belongs to. No coercion; passed positionally and sent verbatim as a path segment.

wire.encoding: Decimal integer path segment; numeric strings are rejected rather than coerced.

parameters.semantics: The entry to update, as the plan's own reply reports it. TestRail identifies a plan entry by a UUID rather than a number, and the driver validates its form before dispatch. No coercion; passed positionally and sent verbatim as a path segment.

wire.encoding: UUID path segment, sent verbatim in the case the caller supplied.

parameters.semantics: No coercion. The JSON object is passed as the driver's payload argument and sent unchanged.

requirements.description: Preserve the object at driver argument 2 as the JSON request body.
Accept an object.
Reject a body that is not an object before driver invocation.
Reject a missing body.

parameters.semantics: The entry's new name, which its runs inherit. No coercion; TestRail owns the format.

requirements.description: Preserve the value under its own name.
Accept a string.
Reject a non-string value before driver invocation.
Send nothing for it when the caller did not supply one.

parameters.semantics: The entry's description. No coercion; TestRail owns the format.

requirements.description: Preserve the value under its own name.
Accept a string.
Reject a non-string value before driver invocation.
Send nothing for it when the caller did not supply one.

parameters.semantics: The user the entry's runs are assigned to. The driver forwards any number, so the boundary holds it to the identifier domain.
Whether the entry's runs cover every case of the suite. TestRail treats a false value and an omitted one differently once case_ids is present, so the flag is forwarded as given.

requirements.description: Preserve the flag under its own name.
Accept true and send it.
Accept false and send it, rather than dropping it as if it were absent.
Reject a numeric stand-in for the boolean before driver invocation.
Send no flag when the caller did not supply one.

parameters.semantics: The cases the entry's runs cover when include_all is false. Narrowing the selection removes the tests that fall outside it, and their results with them. The driver forwards any number, so the boundary holds every member to the identifier domain.

wire.encoding: JSON array of integers under case_ids.

requirements.description: Preserve every member in order under case_ids.
Accept a list of identifiers.
Reject a non-positive member before driver invocation.
Accept an empty array and send it, which is what lets a dynamic filter decide the selection.
Send no list when the caller did not supply one.

parameters.semantics: A selection filter in the form the TestRail interface produces: a mode, which the payload declares as a string rather than a number, and a filters map whose keys name a field such as cases:priority_id. The values are forwarded as given, since TestRail's own examples vary their shape from one field to the next. The object carries nothing beyond those two fields, and an extra one is refused.

wire.encoding: JSON object under dynamic_filters, sent unchanged.

requirements.description: Preserve the filter object under its own name.
Accept a mode and a filters map.
Reject a filter object without its mode before driver invocation.
Reject a numeric mode, which the payload declares as a string.
Send no filter when the caller did not supply one.

parameters.semantics: The entry's start date. Seconds since the Unix epoch, as TestRail documents. The driver forwards any number, so the boundary holds it to the timestamp domain.
The entry's end date. Seconds since the Unix epoch, as TestRail documents. The driver forwards any number, so the boundary holds it to the timestamp domain.
The entry's references. No coercion; TestRail owns the format.

requirements.description: Preserve the value under its own name.
Accept a string.
Reject a non-string value before driver invocation.
Send nothing for it when the caller did not supply one.
